title.es: Las preguntas detrás de la pregunta

es: Reconocer si una pregunta de entrevista es de motivación, de experiencia pasada o hipotética y qué busca el comité.

teaching.en: The panel asks every candidate why they want the scholarship, because a motivation question is designed to reveal genuine reasons rather than a rehearsed speech.
teaching.es: El comité pregunta a cada candidato por qué quiere la beca, porque una pregunta de motivación está pensada para revelar razones auténticas y no un discurso ensayado.
teaching.explanationEs: Why do you want…? es una pregunta de motivación: busca razones reales, no frases memorizadas.
segments: The panel asks every candidate why they want the scholarship, because a motivation
question is designed to reveal genuine reasons rather than a rehearsed speech.
teaching.audioText: The panel asks every candidate why they want the scholarship, because a motivation question is designed to reveal genuine reasons rather than a rehearsed speech.

teaching.en: When a panel member says Tell me about a time when you led a team, the behavioural question aims to assess your track record through a real past event.
teaching.es: Cuando un miembro del comité dice «Cuéntame sobre una vez en que lideraste un equipo», la pregunta de conducta busca evaluar tu trayectoria a través de un hecho real del pasado.
teaching.explanationEs: Tell me about a time when + pasado pide un hecho real. Track record: lo que has demostrado hasta ahora.
segments: When a panel member says Tell me about a time when you led a team,
the behavioural question aims to assess your track record through a real past event.
teaching.audioText: When a panel member says Tell me about a time when you led a team, the behavioural question aims to assess your track record through a real past event.

teaching.en: A hypothetical question such as What would you do if the bus did not arrive? does not test what you have done; it shows how you reason.
teaching.es: Una pregunta hipotética como «¿Qué harías si el autobús no llegara?» no comprueba lo que has hecho; muestra cómo razonas.
teaching.explanationEs: What would you do if + pasado: se responde con would + tu decisión y su motivo.
segments: A hypothetical question such as What would you do if the bus did not
arrive? does not test what you have done; it shows how you reason.
teaching.audioText: A hypothetical question such as What would you do if the bus did not arrive? does not test what you have done; it shows how you reason.

teaching.en: A good candidate names one strength and backs it up with a precise example, because an example is what persuades a panel.
teaching.es: Un buen candidato nombra un punto fuerte y lo respalda con un ejemplo preciso, porque es el ejemplo lo que convence a un comité.
teaching.explanationEs: Strength + example: la cualidad sola no convence; el ejemplo la prueba. Back up: respaldar con pruebas.
segments: A good candidate names one strength and backs it up with
a precise example, because an example is what persuades a panel.
teaching.audioText: A good candidate names one strength and backs it up with a precise example, because an example is what persuades a panel.

teaching.en: Interviewers sometimes use a follow-up question to elicit detail that a polished first answer has left out, so never assume the topic is closed.
teaching.es: Los entrevistadores a veces usan una pregunta de seguimiento para obtener detalles que una primera respuesta pulida ha dejado fuera, así que nunca des el tema por cerrado.
teaching.explanationEs: Elicit detail: conseguir que alguien aporte más información. La pregunta de seguimiento profundiza en tu respuesta.
segments: Interviewers sometimes use a follow-up question to elicit detail that a polished
first answer has left out, so never assume the topic is closed.
teaching.audioText: Interviewers sometimes use a follow-up question to elicit detail that a polished first answer has left out, so never assume the topic is closed.

teaching.en: Before you answer, identify the type of question, because a motivation question calls for a reason, a behavioural one for a story and a hypothetical one for a decision.
teaching.es: Antes de responder, identifica el tipo de pregunta, porque una de motivación pide una razón, una de conducta una historia y una hipotética una decisión.
teaching.explanationEs: Identificar el tipo de pregunta decide la estructura de tu respuesta: razón, historia o decisión con would.
segments: Before you answer, identify the type of question, because a motivation question calls for a
reason, a behavioural one for a story and a hypothetical one for a decision.
teaching.audioText: Before you answer, identify the type of question, because a motivation question calls for a reason, a behavioural one for a story and a hypothetical one for a decision.

prompt.es: Lee la pregunta del comité. ¿De qué tipo es y qué busca?

choices.text: Behavioural: the panel wants a story from your past.
Hypothetical: the panel wants to see how you would decide.
Motivation: the panel wants to know your reasons.

feedback.es: La pregunta empieza por «Why do you want…»: es de motivación y busca razones personales. No pide una historia ni una decisión futura.

hint.es: Mira cómo empieza la pregunta: ¿pide un motivo, un hecho pasado o una decisión imaginaria?

origin.text: The scholarship panel turns to the next candidate and asks: «Why do you want to study abroad rather than at a college in your own country?»

prompt.es: Completa: «Ese fue un gran ejemplo de cómo resolviste un problema en equipo.»

answer.text: example

feedback.es: An example of + gerundio/cómo… es la colocación para algo que ilustra una cualidad; la historia de Mia es la prueba de su capacidad.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo que designa la prueba concreta de una cualidad.

origin.text: Mia answers a behavioural question by telling a short story. The panel member smiles and says, «That was a great ___ of how you solved a problem in a team.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Qué harías si perdieras tus apuntes?»

answer.text: What would you do if you lost your notes

feedback.es: Una pregunta hipotética se forma con What would you do if + pasado; lost your notes es la situación imaginada.

hint.es: Empieza por What would you do y termina con la situación imaginaria.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué buscaba el comité al pedir ese momento concreto.

choices.text: Proof that her interest had led to real action.
A list of the subjects she had studied at school.
A promise about what she would study abroad.

feedback.es: Pedir un momento en que su interés «cambió algo» busca pruebas reales de que su pasión se tradujo en acción, más allá del discurso ensayado.

origin.audio: Sara had prepared carefully for her scholarship interview, but the first question took her by surprise: why did she want the place? She had a rehearsed answer about loving science, yet one panel member smiled and asked her to tell them about a moment when that love had actually changed something. Sara hesitated, then described how she had organised a recycling project at her school, what went wrong in the first month and how she fixed it. Afterwards, the panel asked what she would do if the school stopped supporting the project. She said she would look for a company to help and ask former students for advice.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez. ¿De qué tipo es la última pregunta que le hacen a Sara?

choices.text: Behavioural: it asks for a story about a problem she solved before.
Hypothetical: it asks how she would decide in a future problem.
Motivation: it asks why she wants the scholarship.

feedback.es: «What she would do if…» plantea un problema imaginario y pide una decisión: es hipotética, no de conducta ni de motivación.

origin.audio: Sara had prepared carefully for her scholarship interview, but the first question took her by surprise: why did she want the place? She had a rehearsed answer about loving science, yet one panel member smiled and asked her to tell them about a moment when that love had actually changed something. Sara hesitated, then described how she had organised a recycling project at her school, what went wrong in the first month and how she fixed it. Afterwards, the panel asked what she would do if the school stopped supporting the project. She said she would look for a company to help and ask former students for advice.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada pregunta de entrevista con lo que busca el comité.

pairs: Why do you want this scholarship?
Tell me about a time when you solved a problem.

pairs.es: Un hecho real del pasado, con resultado

pairs: What would you do if a teammate left?

pairs.es: Tu forma de razonar y decidir

pairs: What is your biggest strength?

pairs.es: Una cualidad respaldada con un ejemplo

feedback.es: Cada pregunta persigue una evidencia distinta: razones, hechos pasados, razonamiento o cualidades demostradas.

pairs: Why do you want this scholarship?

pairs.es: Un hecho real del pasado, con resultado

pairs: What would you do if a teammate left?

pairs.es: Tu forma de razonar y decidir

prompt.es: Escucha la pregunta. ¿Qué quiere averiguar realmente el comité?

choices.text: Whether she has ever worked in a group before.
Why she believes she deserves the scholarship.
How she handles failure and learns from it.

feedback.es: Tras oír solo éxitos, el comité pide un fallo y qué hizo después: busca ver cómo gestiona el error y qué aprende, no su experiencia en grupo.

origin.audio: The chair of the panel leaned forward and said: you have told us about your successes, which is good to hear, but tell me about a time when something went wrong, and what you did about it. The candidate paused, then admitted that she had once missed a deadline for a group project because she had taken on too much.

prompt.es: ¿Qué debilidad revela esta respuesta a una pregunta de motivación?

choices.text: It gives a general wish instead of a concrete reason.
It says little about what the candidate has already achieved.
It names a strength but gives no example to support it.

feedback.es: La respuesta se apoya en un deseo general y en lo que «dice todo el mundo», sin ninguna razón concreta. No se pide aquí un logro pasado ni nombra ninguna cualidad.

origin.text: Candidate: Honestly, I have always wanted to travel, and I think the scholarship would be a great opportunity, because studying abroad looks exciting and everyone says that it changes your life.

prompt.es: Completa: «Querían evaluar lo tranquilo que se mantenía bajo presión.»

answer.text: assess

feedback.es: Assess how + oración significa valorar hasta qué punto algo es cierto en alguien; es el verbo de evaluar propio del comité.

origin.text: After each answer, the panel member wrote a few notes. It was clear that the panel was trying to ___ how calm the candidate stayed under pressure.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Cuéntame sobre una vez en que discrepaste de un líder.»

answer.text: Tell me about a time when you disagreed with a leader

feedback.es: Tell me about a time when + pasado introduce una pregunta de conducta; disagreed with a leader es el hecho que se pide contar.

prompt.es: ¿Qué evalúa el comité con esta pregunta y qué espera oír?

choices.text: A real past event told in the simple past.
How the candidate reasons: a decision explained with would.
The reasons why the candidate wants the place.

feedback.es: «Suppose… What would you do…» plantea una situación imaginaria: busca una decisión razonada con would, no un recuerdo ni una motivación.

origin.text: After a long pause, the panel member leans forward and says: «Suppose the group you are working with falls two weeks behind schedule just before a big presentation. What would you do, and what would you tell the team?»

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender la narradora sobre la respuesta de Tom.

choices.text: That it revealed a serious gap in his experience.
That it impressed the panel by being so honest.
That it sounded rehearsed and did not convince the panel.

feedback.es: La narradora sospecha que el comité ya había oído esa respuesta muchas veces: suena ensayada, y por eso no anotan nada.

origin.audio: Afterwards, Tom told me he had felt fine until the panel asked about his worst flaw. He said that he cared too much about his work, and they smiled politely without writing anything down. I suspect they had heard that answer many times before.

prompt.es: Completa: «Decir «soy trabajador» no revela nada útil sobre lo que has hecho.»

answer.text: reveal

feedback.es: Reveal anything about significa dejar ver algo; una cualidad sin ejemplo no descubre nada concreto sobre el candidato.

origin.text: An answer that simply says «I am hard-working» does not ___ anything useful about what you have actually done, so the panel will probably ask a follow-up question.

es: Resumir en una frase las preguntas de una entrevista con enquire about, want to know, be asked to y probe.

teaching.en: Interviewers often enquire about your volunteer work, and you may then be asked to describe one project in enough detail for them to see your part in it.
teaching.es: Los entrevistadores suelen preguntar por tu trabajo de voluntariado, y luego puede que te pidan describir un proyecto con el detalle suficiente para ver cuál fue tu papel.
teaching.explanationEs: Enquire about + nombre resume una pregunta sobre un tema. Be asked to + verbo recoge una petición.
segments: Interviewers often enquire about your volunteer work, and you may then be asked to
describe one project in enough detail for them to see your part in it.
teaching.audioText: Interviewers often enquire about your volunteer work, and you may then be asked to describe one project in enough detail for them to see your part in it.

teaching.en: Interviewers usually want to know whether you can work at weekends, so a short account says that they wanted to know whether I could.
teaching.es: Los entrevistadores suelen querer saber si puedes trabajar los fines de semana, así que un relato breve dice que querían saber si yo podía.
teaching.explanationEs: Want to know + whether + sujeto + verbo: pregunta de sí o no, sin did ni inversión; el tiempo retrocede.
segments: Interviewers usually want to know whether you can work at weekends, so
a short account says that they wanted to know whether I could.
teaching.audioText: Interviewers usually want to know whether you can work at weekends, so a short account says that they wanted to know whether I could.

teaching.en: If a panel decides to probe your reasons, it may query a detail that looked vague in your first answer.
teaching.es: Si un comité decide indagar en tus razones, puede cuestionar un dato que parecía vago en tu primera respuesta.
teaching.explanationEs: Probe es seguir preguntando sobre lo mismo; query pone en duda un dato concreto.
segments: If a panel decides to probe your reasons, it may
query a detail that looked vague in your first answer.
teaching.audioText: If a panel decides to probe your reasons, it may query a detail that looked vague in your first answer.

teaching.en: A concise report keeps the meaning and skips the small talk: They asked why I had applied and how long I had worked there.
teaching.es: Un informe conciso conserva el sentido y omite la charla superficial: Preguntaron por qué había solicitado y cuánto tiempo llevaba trabajando allí.
teaching.explanationEs: Con wh- el orden es afirmativo (why I had applied) y el tiempo retrocede un paso.
segments: A concise report keeps the meaning and skips the small talk: They
asked why I had applied and how long I had worked there.
teaching.audioText: A concise report keeps the meaning and skips the small talk: They asked why I had applied and how long I had worked there.

teaching.en: Some interviewers zero in on a single point and press for details, so after the interview I wrote a short report of each exchange.
teaching.es: Algunos entrevistadores se centran en un solo punto e insisten en pedir detalles, así que después de la entrevista escribí un informe breve de cada intercambio.
teaching.explanationEs: Zero in on + nombre: concentrarse en un punto; press for + nombre: insistir en pedirlo.
segments: Some interviewers zero in on a single point and press for details,
so after the interview I wrote a short report of each exchange.
teaching.audioText: Some interviewers zero in on a single point and press for details, so after the interview I wrote a short report of each exchange.

teaching.en: When a panel decides to delve into your motives, your report should name the topic first and then say what they wanted to know about it.
teaching.es: Cuando un comité decide profundizar en tus motivos, tu informe debe nombrar primero el tema y luego decir qué querían saber sobre él.
teaching.explanationEs: Delve into + nombre: profundizar en un asunto. El informe ordena tema y pregunta.
segments: When a panel decides to delve into your motives, your report should name
the topic first and then say what they wanted to know about it.
teaching.audioText: When a panel decides to delve into your motives, your report should name the topic first and then say what they wanted to know about it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Querían saber si podía trabajar los fines de semana.»

answer.text: whether

feedback.es: Las preguntas de sí o no se cuentan con whether o if + sujeto + verbo, sin did ni inversión; el verbo retrocede a could.

hint.es: Es la palabra que introduce una pregunta de sí o no dentro de una frase; if también sirve.

origin.text: After the interview, Tom's mother asks what the panel was interested in. Tom answers, «They wanted to know ___ I could work at weekends.»

prompt.es: ¿Cómo se resume la pregunta del comité en una sola frase?

choices.text: They enquired about my experience of working with children.
They enquired about what was my experience of working with children.
They wanted to know that my experience of working with children was.

feedback.es: Enquire about + nombre resume la pregunta sobre un tema en un solo verbo. Las otras conservan la inversión o usan that en lugar de una pregunta indirecta.

hint.es: Busca el verbo que va seguido directamente del tema, sin repetir la pregunta entera.

origin.text: The scholarship panel turned to Mia and asked: «What is your experience of working with children?» Later, she had to report the question to her teacher.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me pidieron que describiera un proyecto con detalle.»

answer.text: I was asked to describe one project in detail

feedback.es: Be asked to + verbo base recoge una petición en voz pasiva: I was asked to describe… resume la orden del comité.

hint.es: Empieza por I was asked y continúa con el verbo base.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué querían saber en segundo lugar sobre Leo.

choices.text: Why he preferred teaching at night.
Whether he was available to work at night.
How long he had taught in total.

feedback.es: Primero preguntaron por su experiencia docente y en segundo lugar quisieron saber si podía trabajar de noche. No preguntaron por preferencias ni por años.

origin.audio: After the interview, Leo told us what the panel had wanted to know. First, they enquired about his experience of teaching, and then they wanted to know whether he could work at night. After that, he was asked to describe the most difficult class he had ever taught. When he answered, one panel member probed his decision to change the lesson plan halfway through, asking why he had waited so long. Leo said that, looking back, he should have asked for help earlier. Overall, he felt that the questions had been fair, although the last one had made him nervous.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez. ¿Qué hizo el miembro del comité que «probed» su decisión?

choices.text: He asked Leo to repeat his first answer.
He offered to help Leo to write a better lesson plan.
He asked Leo to justify a decision he had made.

feedback.es: Indagar en la decisión de cambiar el plan es seguir preguntando por qué esperó tanto: le pide que la justifique, no que repita ni le ofrece ayuda.

origin.audio: After the interview, Leo told us what the panel had wanted to know. First, they enquired about his experience of teaching, and then they wanted to know whether he could work at night. After that, he was asked to describe the most difficult class he had ever taught. When he answered, one panel member probed his decision to change the lesson plan halfway through, asking why he had waited so long. Leo said that, looking back, he should have asked for help earlier. Overall, he felt that the questions had been fair, although the last one had made him nervous.

prompt.es: Completa: «Querían preguntar por mi experiencia de trabajo en el extranjero.»

answer.text: enquire

feedback.es: Enquire about + nombre es el verbo de informe para preguntar por un tema; tras wished to va la forma base.

origin.text: In my notes for the tutor I wrote that the panel wished to ___ about my experience of working abroad, and that they did not ask anything about my studies.

prompt.es: Resume en una frase cada una de las tres preguntas del comité.

answer.text: They wanted to know why I had chosen that course. They asked whether I could start in May. I was asked to describe my last job.
accepted: They wanted to know why I had chosen that course. They asked whether I could start in May. I was asked to describe my last job.
The panel enquired why I had chosen the course and whether I could start in May, and I was asked to describe my last job.

feedback.es: Las tres frases cuentan la pregunta con estilo indirecto: why + orden afirmativo, whether + could y be asked to + verbo.

origin.text: El comité te hizo tres preguntas: 1) «Why did you choose this course?» 2) «Can you start in May?» 3) «Describe your last job.» Cuéntalas después en pasado, una frase cada una, con estilo indirecto.

evidenceGroups: whether I could start in May
if I could start in May
whether I was able to start in May
if I was able to start in May
asked to describe my last job
asked me to describe my last job
asked to describe my previous job
asked me to describe my previous job
wanted me to describe my last job
told me to describe my last job
asked me to tell them about my last job

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender este relato sobre el interés del comité?

choices.text: That it wanted proof that the candidate had led others, not just experience.
That it cared about results more than about the candidate's own role.
That it wanted to know how long the candidate had volunteered.

feedback.es: Insistir en si había liderado un equipo indica que busca pruebas concretas de liderazgo, no experiencia general; el comité no cuestiona el voluntariado ni pregunta por su duración, y el papel de la candidata es justo lo que explora.

origin.text: The panel enquired about my volunteer work for ten minutes and wanted to know whether I had ever led a team. When I described my project, one member probed my reasons, and I was asked to explain why I had not asked for help.

prompt.es: Escucha la pregunta del comité y elige el informe más fiel.

choices.text: They wanted to know that I could start in September and what prevented me.
They wanted to know whether I would be able to start in September and what would stop me.
They asked me could I start in September and what would prevent me from coming.

feedback.es: El informe fiel usa whether + would be able y what would stop me con orden afirmativo; las otras mantienen la inversión o cambian la pregunta en una afirmación.

origin.audio: Could you tell us whether you would be able to start in September and, if not, what would prevent you from doing so?

prompt.es: Ordena: «El comité preguntó por mis planes después del curso.»

answer.text: The panel enquired about my plans after the course

feedback.es: Enquire about + nombre resume la pregunta: the panel enquired about my plans, y after the course precisa el momento.

prompt.es: Mia debe contar las dos preguntas a su profesor. ¿Qué informe es fiel?

choices.text: They wanted to know how long did I work with children and why did I leave my previous post.
They enquired about how long have I worked with children and why I left my previous post.
They wanted to know how long I had worked with children and why I had left my previous post.

feedback.es: Las dos preguntas se cuentan con orden afirmativo y un paso atrás: have worked pasa a had worked y did you leave a had left. Las otras mantienen la inversión.

origin.text: Original questions from the panel: «How long have you worked with children? Why did you leave your previous post?» Mia must now report both questions to her teacher in one sentence.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué sugiere sobre cómo se sintió Carlos.

choices.text: That the constant questions put him under pressure.
That he thought the panel was poorly prepared.
That he felt relaxed because the questions were predictable.

feedback.es: Carlos dice que el comité «no dejaba de presionarle» con preguntas cada vez más concretas: se sintió bajo presión por su insistencia, no orgulloso ni crítico con su preparación.

origin.audio: After the interview, Carlos complained that the panel had kept pressing him. They enquired about his reasons for leaving his last job, then they wanted to know whether the company had asked him to go, and finally one of them probed his answer by asking why he had not mentioned it in his application.

prompt.es: Completa: «El entrevistador insistió en pedir más detalles del proyecto.»

answer.text: for

feedback.es: Press for + nombre es la colocación para insistir en pedir algo; con on significaría presionar sobre una persona o un asunto.

origin.text: I gave a vague answer, so the interviewer decided to press ___ more details about the project before moving on to the next question.

es: Comprobar si el relato de una entrevista es fiel a las preguntas originales y detectar cuándo omite, exagera o distorsiona.

vocabulary.es: citar mal, citar de forma inexacta
exagerar, dar más importancia de la debida

teaching.en: A faithful report keeps the meaning of the original question, even when the words change, because it is the intention that has to survive.
teaching.es: Un informe fiel conserva el sentido de la pregunta original, aunque cambien las palabras, porque lo que tiene que sobrevivir es la intención.
teaching.explanationEs: Fiel no es copiar: es conservar el sentido. Original es la pregunta tal como se formuló.
segments: A faithful report keeps the meaning of the original question, even when
the words change, because it is the intention that has to survive.
teaching.audioText: A faithful report keeps the meaning of the original question, even when the words change, because it is the intention that has to survive.

teaching.en: If the panel only asked for an example, saying that they chose to challenge his answer would distort what really happened.
teaching.es: Si el comité solo pidió un ejemplo, decir que decidió cuestionar su respuesta distorsionaría lo que realmente ocurrió.
teaching.explanationEs: Challenge es poner en duda; pedir un ejemplo no lo es. Distort cambia el sentido.
segments: If the panel only asked for an example, saying that they
chose to challenge his answer would distort what really happened.
teaching.audioText: If the panel only asked for an example, saying that they chose to challenge his answer would distort what really happened.

teaching.en: Do not omit the condition: the panel asked whether he could work on Saturdays, but only in the morning, and leaving that out changes the question.
teaching.es: No omitas la condición: el comité preguntó si podía trabajar los sábados, pero solo por la mañana, y dejar eso fuera cambia la pregunta.
teaching.explanationEs: Omit: dejar fuera un dato; aquí la condición only in the morning cambia la pregunta.
segments: Do not omit the condition: the panel asked whether he could work on
Saturdays, but only in the morning, and leaving that out changes the question.
teaching.audioText: Do not omit the condition: the panel asked whether he could work on Saturdays, but only in the morning, and leaving that out changes the question.

teaching.en: To say that the panel demanded an answer would exaggerate the situation, and to claim that they were furious would overstate it even further.
teaching.es: Decir que el comité exigió una respuesta exageraría la situación, y afirmar que estaban furiosos la exageraría todavía más.
teaching.explanationEs: Exaggerate y overstate suben el grado: convierten una pregunta en una exigencia o un enfado.
segments: To say that the panel demanded an answer would exaggerate the situation,
and to claim that they were furious would overstate it even further.
teaching.audioText: To say that the panel demanded an answer would exaggerate the situation, and to claim that they were furious would overstate it even further.

teaching.en: Adding details that nobody mentioned is a way to embellish a story, and quoting half a sentence to change its point is a way to misquote the speaker.
teaching.es: Añadir detalles que nadie mencionó es una forma de adornar una historia, y citar media frase para cambiar su sentido es una forma de citar mal a quien habla.
teaching.explanationEs: Embellish añade detalles inventados; misquote altera lo que alguien dijo realmente.
segments: Adding details that nobody mentioned is a way to embellish a story, and quoting
half a sentence to change its point is a way to misquote the speaker.
teaching.audioText: Adding details that nobody mentioned is a way to embellish a story, and quoting half a sentence to change its point is a way to misquote the speaker.

teaching.en: An accurate report chooses its verb with care: the panel may ask, enquire or press, and each verb implies a different degree of insistence, so never quote a remark out of context.
teaching.es: Un informe preciso elige con cuidado el verbo: el comité puede preguntar, consultar o insistir, y cada verbo implica un grado distinto, así que nunca cites un comentario fuera de contexto.
teaching.explanationEs: Ask es neutro; enquire about introduce un tema; press añade insistencia. Out of context: sin lo que lo rodeaba.
segments: An accurate report chooses its verb with care: the panel may ask, enquire or press, and
each verb implies a different degree of insistence, so never quote a remark out of context.
teaching.audioText: An accurate report chooses its verb with care: the panel may ask, enquire or press, and each verb implies a different degree of insistence, so never quote a remark out of context.

prompt.es: ¿Es fiel este informe a la pregunta original? Elige la valoración correcta.

choices.text: No: the question type changes from yes or no to why.
Yes: the meaning is kept and the tense moves back one step.
No: a condition has been left out of the original question by mistake.

feedback.es: Conserva el tipo de pregunta (sí o no) y retrocede el tiempo de did enjoy a had enjoyed: es fiel. No añade ni omite nada.

hint.es: Compara el tipo de pregunta, el contenido y el tiempo verbal entre el original y el informe.

origin.text: Leo is interviewed for a place at a language school. The interviewer asks him: «Did you enjoy the course?» Later, Leo tells his sister: «They asked me whether I had enjoyed the course.»

prompt.es: ¿Qué defecto tiene este informe del día de la entrevista?

choices.text: It omits the date mentioned by the manager.
It changes the person who asked the question.
It exaggerates: a question becomes a demand.

feedback.es: La pregunta «Can you start…?» se convierte en una exigencia con enfado añadido: el informe exagera el grado.

hint.es: Mira el verbo de reporte: ¿una pregunta es lo mismo que una exigencia?

origin.text: Original question from the manager: «Can you start in June?» Report that Carlos gave to his friends: «The manager demanded that I start in June, and he was not happy about it.»

prompt.es: Completa: «Me preguntaron si podía empezar en junio.»

answer.text: could

feedback.es: En el informe can retrocede un paso a could; la pregunta de sí o no se mantiene con if.

hint.es: Es la forma pasada de can.

origin.text: The manager had asked Leo, «Can you start in June?» That evening Leo told his father, «They asked me if I ___ start in June.»

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué defecto tiene el primer informe de Sam.

choices.text: It changes the question: yes or no becomes why.
It makes the question sound like an order.
It matches what the interviewer really asked.

feedback.es: La pregunta original era de sí o no y Sam la cuenta como una pregunta con why: cambia su tipo y, con él, su sentido.

origin.audio: Sam's interview lasted twenty minutes. At the start, the interviewer looked at him and asked: can you start next week? Later that evening, Sam told his father that the interviewer had asked him why he wanted to start next week. Then he said that she had demanded that he finish his degree before September, although in fact she had only asked whether he thought he could manage both. His father sighed and said that Sam's version did not sound like the same interview.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez. ¿Qué defecto tiene el segundo informe de Sam sobre sus estudios?

choices.text: It changes a yes-or-no question into a why-question.
It turns a cautious question into a demand.
It makes the question sound easier than it was.

feedback.es: La entrevistadora solo preguntó si podría con ambas cosas; Sam dice que exigió terminar antes de septiembre. Convierte una pregunta prudente en una exigencia; el cambio a why es del primer informe.

origin.audio: Sam's interview lasted twenty minutes. At the start, the interviewer looked at him and asked: can you start next week? Later that evening, Sam told his father that the interviewer had asked him why he wanted to start next week. Then he said that she had demanded that he finish his degree before September, although in fact she had only asked whether he thought he could manage both. His father sighed and said that Sam's version did not sound like the same interview.

prompt.es: Original: «¿Puedes trabajar los fines de semana?» Valora cada informe.

pairs: They demanded that I work at weekends.

pairs.es: Exagera: una pregunta pasa a exigencia

pairs: They asked whether I could work.

pairs.es: Omite un dato: los fines de semana

pairs: They asked why I work at weekends.
They asked whether I could work at weekends.

feedback.es: Cada informe falla de una manera distinta: exagera el grado, omite un dato o cambia el tipo de pregunta; solo uno conserva todo.

pairs: They demanded that I work at weekends.

pairs.es: Exagera: una pregunta pasa a exigencia

pairs: They asked whether I could work.

pairs.es: Omite un dato: los fines de semana

pairs: They asked why I work at weekends.
They asked whether I could work at weekends.

prompt.es: Escucha y decide qué defecto tiene el informe de la candidata.

choices.text: It changes the question from yes or no to why.
It exaggerates how much the panel wanted Saturdays.
It leaves out the condition about the mornings.

feedback.es: El informe conserva la pregunta de sí o no y su tiempo verbal, pero omite la condición («only in the mornings»), que cambia lo que se pregunta.

origin.audio: The panel asked whether she could work on Saturdays, but only in the mornings, because the afternoons were already full. When her friend asked her about the interview, she said: they asked me if I could work on Saturdays. Her friend nodded, but the panel would hardly have recognised that version of its own question.

prompt.es: ¿Qué hace este informe con el tono del original?

choices.text: It turns a neutral invitation into criticism and an order.
It faithfully passes on a polite suggestion made by the interviewer.
It leaves out the subject of the original question.

feedback.es: El original es una invitación neutra; el informe la convierte en reproche («lacked») y obligación («must»): distorsiona el tono.

origin.text: Interviewer: «You haven't mentioned any experience abroad. Is that something you would like to develop?» Candidate's later report to a friend: «He told me that I lacked experience abroad and that I must develop it.»

prompt.es: Completa: «El informe no copió las palabras, pero fue totalmente fiel a su sentido.»

answer.text: faithful

feedback.es: Be faithful to + nombre: mantenerse fiel al sentido; un informe puede cambiar las palabras y seguir siendo fiel.

origin.text: The report did not copy a single word of the question, yet it was completely ___ to its meaning, so the panel would have recognised it at once.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me preguntaron cuánto tiempo había vivido en el extranjero.»

answer.text: They asked me how long I had lived abroad

feedback.es: How long + had lived: la pregunta «How long have you lived abroad?» retrocede al pasado perfecto y mantiene el orden afirmativo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué ha perdido este informe respecto a la pregunta original?

choices.text: The tense: the original was in the past, so the report should use had.
The reason: a why-question became a yes-or-no question.
A condition: the original added a limit that the report omitted.

feedback.es: La pregunta pedía un motivo (why); el informe la reduce a sí o no y pierde justo lo que el comité quería saber.

origin.text: Original: «Why are you interested in this school?» Report: «They asked me if I was interested in the school.» Ana, who had been in the room, said that the report sounded polite but had lost something important.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué ilustra esta historia.

choices.text: How panels often suspect candidates of lying about their experience.
How references are usually checked before interviews.
How retelling can turn a neutral question into blame.

feedback.es: La petición rutinaria de una referencia se convirtió en un cargo grave al contarla: la historia muestra cómo el relato distorsiona una pregunta neutra.

origin.audio: When my sister described her interview, she said the panel had practically accused her of lying about her experience. But when I read the notes she had sent me afterwards, the question was simply whether she could provide a reference for that job. Somewhere between the room and the retelling, a routine request had been turned into a serious charge.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si omites la condición, el informe ya no será preciso.»

answer.text: omit

feedback.es: Omit the condition: dejar fuera un dato relevante; aunque la frase suene razonable, deja de ser un relato exacto.

origin.text: If you ___ the condition from the original question, your report will sound reasonable, but it will no longer be an accurate account of what was asked.

es: Responder una pregunta de conducta con situación, acción, resultado y lección, y una hipotética con would, un motivo y un ejemplo.

vocabulary.es: estar a la altura del reto

teaching.en: When the club lost its hall, I took the initiative and asked the library for a room, instead of waiting for someone else to solve the problem.
teaching.es: Cuando el club perdió su sala, tomé la iniciativa y pedí una sala a la biblioteca, en lugar de esperar a que otro resolviera el problema.
teaching.explanationEs: Respuesta de conducta: situación y acción en pasado simple (lost, asked). Take the initiative: actuar sin que te lo pidan.
segments: When the club lost its hall, I took the initiative and asked the library
for a room, instead of waiting for someone else to solve the problem.
teaching.audioText: When the club lost its hall, I took the initiative and asked the library for a room, instead of waiting for someone else to solve the problem.

teaching.en: I can handle complaints because I have done it before, and I often draw on what I learned during the year I worked in the school shop.
teaching.es: Sé gestionar las quejas porque ya lo he hecho antes, y a menudo recurro a lo que aprendí durante el año que trabajé en la tienda del colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: Present perfect (have done) para la experiencia general; pasado simple para el detalle (worked). Draw on: apoyarse en algo.
segments: I can handle complaints because I have done it before, and I often draw
on what I learned during the year I worked in the school shop.
teaching.audioText: I can handle complaints because I have done it before, and I often draw on what I learned during the year I worked in the school shop.

teaching.en: As a result, the club kept its Tuesday meetings, and that was exactly the outcome I had hoped for when I first approached the library.
teaching.es: Como resultado, el club mantuvo sus reuniones de los martes, y ese era exactamente el resultado que yo esperaba cuando me dirigí por primera vez a la biblioteca.
teaching.explanationEs: As a result + pasado: cierra la historia con su efecto. Outcome es el resultado final.
segments: As a result, the club kept its Tuesday meetings, and that was exactly
the outcome I had hoped for when I first approached the library.
teaching.audioText: As a result, the club kept its Tuesday meetings, and that was exactly the outcome I had hoped for when I first approached the library.

teaching.en: That experience taught me an important lesson: when a problem appears, take ownership of it early and ask for help before it grows.
teaching.es: Aquella experiencia me enseñó una lección importante: cuando aparece un problema, asume la responsabilidad pronto y pide ayuda antes de que crezca.
teaching.explanationEs: Taught me a lesson: la enseñanza cierra la respuesta de conducta. Take ownership of + nombre: hacerte cargo.
segments: That experience taught me an important lesson: when a problem appears, take
ownership of it early and ask for help before it grows.
teaching.audioText: That experience taught me an important lesson: when a problem appears, take ownership of it early and ask for help before it grows.

teaching.en: In that case, I would first weigh up the options, speak to the leader and then ask the team for evidence before deciding anything.
teaching.es: En ese caso, primero sopesaría las opciones, hablaría con el líder y luego pediría pruebas al equipo antes de decidir nada.
teaching.explanationEs: Hipótesis: would + verbo base; se responde con una decisión y su razón. In that case conecta con la situación imaginada.
segments: In that case, I would first weigh up the options, speak to
the leader and then ask the team for evidence before deciding anything.
teaching.audioText: In that case, I would first weigh up the options, speak to the leader and then ask the team for evidence before deciding anything.

teaching.en: It would depend on the problem, but I would rise to the challenge and handle it calmly, because a hypothetical answer should show your reasoning.
teaching.es: Dependería del problema, pero estaría a la altura y lo gestionaría con calma, porque una respuesta hipotética debe mostrar tu razonamiento.
teaching.explanationEs: It would depend on… es la salida honesta cuando faltan datos; rise to the challenge: afrontar un reto con solvencia.
segments: It would depend on the problem, but I would rise to the challenge
and handle it calmly, because a hypothetical answer should show your reasoning.
teaching.audioText: It would depend on the problem, but I would rise to the challenge and handle it calmly, because a hypothetical answer should show your reasoning.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mia no esperó órdenes: reservó la sala ella misma. Tomó la iniciativa.»

answer.text: initiative

feedback.es: Take the initiative: actuar por tu cuenta ante un problema; Mia no espera instrucciones, reserva la sala ella misma.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo que describe actuar por cuenta propia, sin esperar órdenes.

origin.text: When the club lost its hall, Mia did not wait to be asked: she called the library herself and booked a room. In other words, she took the ___.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase cierra bien la respuesta a una pregunta de conducta?

choices.text: I have always been a very organised and responsible person, and that is who I am.
I would ask for help early if I ever had to deal with a similar problem.
As a result, we kept the hall, and I learned to ask for help early.

feedback.es: Una respuesta de conducta termina con el resultado (as a result) y la lección. Las otras dos describen un rasgo general o una hipótesis, no lo ocurrido.

hint.es: Busca la frase que cuenta el efecto real de lo que hizo y la enseñanza que sacó.

origin.text: Interviewer: «Tell me about a time when you solved a problem at school.» The candidate has described the situation and what she did. Now she needs one final sentence to finish her answer.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Como resultado, el club mantuvo sus reuniones de los martes.»

answer.text: As a result the club kept its Tuesday meetings

feedback.es: As a result + sujeto + pasado simple: presenta el efecto real de la acción, último paso de la historia.

hint.es: Empieza por la expresión que introduce el resultado y termina con lo que se mantuvo.

prompt.es: Escucha la respuesta y elige cuál fue el resultado de la historia.

choices.text: They raised enough to buy furniture for the library.
They sold two hundred books but raised very little.
The library finally agreed to lend them its hall.

feedback.es: Con la venta reunieron dinero suficiente para una estantería nueva para la biblioteca; se vendieron doscientos libros y la biblioteca no les prestó el salón.

origin.audio: Last year I organised a book sale at my school. When the library told us that it could not lend us the hall, I went to the local café myself and asked it to host the sale instead. We sold two hundred books in one afternoon, and as a result we raised enough money to buy a new shelf for the library. What I learned is that people are usually willing to help if you ask clearly and early. If I were in the same situation again, I would contact the café even sooner.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué lección extrae la hablante.

choices.text: That cafés are better venues than school halls.
That clear, early requests usually receive help.
That organising alone is better than asking others.

feedback.es: La lección es que la gente suele ayudar si se le pide con claridad y pronto; ni compara cafés con salones ni recomienda organizar sin ayuda.

origin.audio: Last year I organised a book sale at my school. When the library told us that it could not lend us the hall, I went to the local café myself and asked it to host the sale instead. We sold two hundred books in one afternoon, and as a result we raised enough money to buy a new shelf for the library. What I learned is that people are usually willing to help if you ask clearly and early. If I were in the same situation again, I would contact the café even sooner.

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta a la pregunta hipotética está bien formulada?

choices.text: I will speak to my teammate first, ask what went wrong and offer help.
I spoke to my teammate first, asked what went wrong and offered help.
I would speak to my teammate first, ask what went wrong and offer help.

feedback.es: Una pregunta hipotética se responde con would + verbo base. Will y el pasado simple hablan de un hecho futuro cierto o de algo ya ocurrido.

origin.text: The interviewer says: «Imagine that one of your teammates misses an important deadline two days before a presentation. What would you do?»

prompt.es: Escribe dos respuestas: una de conducta y una hipotética.

answer.text: Last year, our school football team had no coach, so I took the initiative. I asked a teacher for help, and together we organised the training timetable for all the players. As a result, the team played every match, and I learned that asking for help early solves most problems. If a volunteer did not come to an event, I would speak to that person first, because I would want to understand what had happened. In that case, I would find another volunteer quickly, so that the event could start on time and the guests would not notice the problem. It would depend on the reason, but I would always stay calm, weigh up the options and handle the situation politely, because the outcome matters more than finding someone to blame.
accepted: Last year, our school football team had no coach, so I took the initiative. I asked a teacher for help, and together we organised the training timetable for all the players. As a result, the team played every match, and I learned that asking for help early solves most problems. If a volunteer did not come to an event, I would speak to that person first, because I would want to understand what had happened. In that case, I would find another volunteer quickly, so that the event could start on time and the guests would not notice the problem. It would depend on the reason, but I would always stay calm, weigh up the options and handle the situation politely, because the outcome matters more than finding someone to blame.

Last year, the football team at my school had no coach, so I took the initiative and asked a teacher to help us. I also made a timetable for all the players, and we trained twice a week. As a result, we played every match, and that experience taught me a lesson: it is better to ask for help early than to wait until the situation gets worse. In the second case, if a volunteer did not come to an event, I would call that person first to find out what had happened. In that case, I would ask someone else to take the place, so that the event could start on time and the guests would not notice the problem. It would depend on the reason, but I would weigh up the options and handle it calmly, because a good outcome is more useful than an argument.

feedback.es: La respuesta de conducta cubre situación, acción, resultado y lección en pasado; la hipotética usa would, un motivo y It would depend.

origin.text: Preguntas de una entrevista de voluntariado. 1) «Tell me about a time when you solved a problem in a group.» Datos: el año pasado el equipo de fútbol de tu colegio no tenía entrenador; pediste ayuda a un profesor y organizaste los horarios de entrenamiento; resultado: el equipo jugó todos los partidos; aprendiste que pedir ayuda pronto resuelve problemas. 2) «What would you do if a volunteer did not come to an event?» Responde con would: hablarías primero con esa persona, buscarías a otro voluntario, sopesarías las opciones y dependería del motivo.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué actitud transmite la hablante con su última frase.

choices.text: That people's feelings matter more to her than the product.
That she regrets not having more bread in the shop that day.
That she thinks customers should be more patient.

feedback.es: Decir que escuchar importó más que el pan indica que prioriza el trato al cliente sobre el producto; no lamenta la falta de pan ni reprocha nada al cliente.

origin.audio: Tell me about a time when you handled a difficult situation. Well, last summer a customer became angry because the shop had no bread left. I listened without interrupting, offered him a different loaf and apologised. He thanked me and came back the next day. Looking back, I realise that listening first mattered more than the bread.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tom decidió asumir su propio error en lugar de culpar a otros.»

answer.text: ownership

feedback.es: Take ownership of + nombre es la colocación para asumir la responsabilidad de algo propio en lugar de repartir culpas.

origin.text: When the project was about to fall apart because of a wrong estimate, Tom decided to take ___ of his own mistake instead of blaming his colleagues, and that decision earned him the team's respect.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Si el equipo discrepara, sopesaría ambas opciones.»

answer.text: If the team disagreed I would weigh up both options

feedback.es: If + pasado, would + verbo base: hipótesis con decisión; weigh up both options explica cómo decidirías.

prompt.es: ¿Qué le falta a esta respuesta de conducta para estar completa?

choices.text: The situation and the actions that were taken by the candidate.
The result and what the candidate learned from it.
A hypothetical decision about a future exam.

feedback.es: La respuesta ya tiene situación y acciones, pero se queda sin resultado ni lección: no dice cómo acabó ni qué aprendió.

origin.text: Question: «Tell me about a time when you worked under pressure.» Answer: «Last May I had three exams in one week, so I made a detailed revision plan and asked my sister to test me every evening. I also stopped seeing my friends until the exams were over.»

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué prioridad revela la respuesta de la candidata.

choices.text: Protecting the team from any further client requests.
Delivering exactly what the client asks, whatever the cost.
Keeping the client involved without risking the deadline.

feedback.es: Ofrece un cambio menor a tiempo para que el cliente conserve algo de control sin arriesgar el plazo: prioriza la relación con el cliente y la entrega.

origin.audio: What would you do if a client asked for a change on the last day? Well, it would depend on the change, but I would explain the limits of the project first, and then I would offer a smaller change that we could deliver on time. That way, the client would keep some control, and we would avoid a last-minute mistake.

prompt.es: Escribe la frase de resultado y lección de tu historia.

answer.text: As a result, the group finished on time, and I learned to plan more carefully.
accepted: As a result, the group finished on time, and I learned to plan more carefully.
As a consequence, we completed the project on time, and that taught me to plan better.

feedback.es: La frase une el resultado (as a result + pasado) con la lección aprendida sobre planificar.

origin.text: Cierra tu historia: como resultado, el grupo terminó a tiempo y tú aprendiste a planificar con más cuidado.

es: Responder una entrevista simulada de cinco preguntas, contar después qué te preguntaron con estilo indirecto y valorar tus respuestas.

vocabulary.es: no alcanzar, quedarse corto respecto a

teaching.en: Overall, the panel asked five questions: one about my motivation, two about my experience and two hypothetical ones, so I had to adapt my answers quickly.
teaching.es: En general, el comité hizo cinco preguntas: una sobre mi motivación, dos sobre mi experiencia y dos hipotéticas, así que tuve que adaptar mis respuestas rápidamente.
teaching.explanationEs: Las cinco preguntas reúnen los tres tipos del bloque. Overall abre una valoración de conjunto.
segments: Overall, the panel asked five questions: one about my motivation, two about my
experience and two hypothetical ones, so I had to adapt my answers quickly.
teaching.audioText: Overall, the panel asked five questions: one about my motivation, two about my experience and two hypothetical ones, so I had to adapt my answers quickly.

teaching.en: They wanted to know whether I felt nervous, and I said that I felt confident after the first answer, although I did stumble over one date.
teaching.es: Querían saber si me sentía nervioso, y dije que me sentía seguro tras la primera respuesta, aunque sí me trabé con una fecha.
teaching.explanationEs: Wanted to know whether + pasado para lo que preguntaron; said that + pasado para lo que respondí. Stumble over: trabarse al hablar.
segments: They wanted to know whether I felt nervous, and I said that I
felt confident after the first answer, although I did stumble over one date.
teaching.audioText: They wanted to know whether I felt nervous, and I said that I felt confident after the first answer, although I did stumble over one date.

teaching.en: I was asked to name one weakness, and I explained how I am working on it instead of pretending that I had no room for improvement.
teaching.es: Me pidieron que nombrara un punto débil, y expliqué cómo trabajo en ello en lugar de fingir que no tenía margen de mejora.
teaching.explanationEs: Be asked to + verbo resume la petición. Room for improvement: lo que aún se puede mejorar.
segments: I was asked to name one weakness, and I explained how I am
working on it instead of pretending that I had no room for improvement.
teaching.audioText: I was asked to name one weakness, and I explained how I am working on it instead of pretending that I had no room for improvement.

teaching.en: On reflection, I kept my composure better in the second answer, because it was built around one clear example and I knew exactly where it was going.
teaching.es: Pensándolo bien, mantuve mejor la compostura en la segunda respuesta, porque giraba en torno a un ejemplo claro y sabía exactamente adónde iba.
teaching.explanationEs: On reflection abre una valoración personal; because explica el motivo. Keep your composure: mantener la serenidad.
segments: On reflection, I kept my composure better in the second answer, because it was
built around one clear example and I knew exactly where it was going.
teaching.audioText: On reflection, I kept my composure better in the second answer, because it was built around one clear example and I knew exactly where it was going.

teaching.en: Next time I aim to improve my answer to the hypothetical question by adding a reason, since my first attempt may fall short of what the panel expects.
teaching.es: La próxima vez me propongo mejorar mi respuesta a la pregunta hipotética añadiendo un motivo, ya que mi primer intento puede no alcanzar lo que el comité espera.
teaching.explanationEs: Aim to + verbo base: un objetivo concreto de mejora. Fall short of + nombre: no llegar a lo esperado.
segments: Next time I aim to improve my answer to the hypothetical question by adding
a reason, since my first attempt may fall short of what the panel expects.
teaching.audioText: Next time I aim to improve my answer to the hypothetical question by adding a reason, since my first attempt may fall short of what the panel expects.

teaching.en: Good self-evaluation welcomes constructive criticism without making excuses: it says what went well, what did not and how you will improve.
teaching.es: Una buena autoevaluación acoge la crítica constructiva sin poner excusas: dice qué salió bien, qué no y cómo vas a mejorar.
teaching.explanationEs: Constructive criticism señala qué cambiar y cómo; una autoevaluación útil termina con un plan.
segments: Good self-evaluation welcomes constructive criticism without making excuses: it says what
went well, what did not and how you will improve.
teaching.audioText: Good self-evaluation welcomes constructive criticism without making excuses: it says what went well, what did not and how you will improve.

prompt.es: Después del simulacro, Sara se escribe una nota. ¿Qué frase es una autoevaluación útil?

choices.text: On reflection, my answer was short, so next time I aim to add an example.
My answer was terrible, and I am clearly not a good candidate for this scholarship.
The panel was unfair and never listened to anything that I wanted to say.

feedback.es: Una autoevaluación útil valora lo ocurrido (on reflection) y fija una mejora concreta (aim to). Las otras dos solo se lamentan o culpan al comité.

hint.es: Busca la frase que reconoce un fallo concreto y propone qué hacer la próxima vez.

origin.text: After her mock interview, Sara writes a short note to herself so that she can prepare better for the real one. She wants the note to be honest but also useful.

prompt.es: Completa: «Dije que me sentía seguro tras la primera respuesta.»

answer.text: confident

feedback.es: Feel confident describe seguridad en uno mismo; en el informe el tiempo retrocede: I felt confident tras said that.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo que significa seguro de uno mismo.

origin.text: The panel had asked whether Ana felt anxious about the interview. She remembers: «I said that I felt ___ after the first answer, because I knew my example well.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me pidieron que nombrara un punto débil y lo explicara.»

answer.text: I was asked to name one weakness and explain it

feedback.es: Be asked to + verbo base resume una petición; name one weakness and explain it son las dos acciones que se piden.

hint.es: Empieza por I was asked y continúa con los dos verbos.

prompt.es: Escucha el informe y elige qué querían saber en segundo lugar.

choices.text: Why she wanted to travel in the summer.
Whether she could travel during the summer.
How long she had volunteered at the shelter.

feedback.es: Lo segundo que quisieron saber fue si podía viajar en verano (whether); no preguntaron el motivo ni cuánto tiempo llevaba de voluntaria.

origin.audio: They asked me three questions. First, they enquired about my volunteer work at the animal shelter. Second, they wanted to know whether I could travel during the summer, which surprised me a little because I had not mentioned it in my application. Finally, I was asked to describe a problem I had solved, and I talked about the night the shelter flooded. I felt nervous at the start, but by the last question I felt relaxed, and I even managed to joke about the wet dogs.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez. ¿Por qué le sorprendió esa segunda pregunta?

choices.text: She had expected a question about the flood instead.
She thought the panel already knew her availability.
She had not mentioned travelling in her application.

feedback.es: Le sorprendió porque no había mencionado el viaje en su solicitud. La inundación se cuenta después, como respuesta a la tercera pregunta.

prompt.es: Escribe el relato de tu entrevista y una autoevaluación breve.

answer.text: The panel asked me five questions. First, they wanted to know why I wanted the scholarship, and I explained my motivation. Second, I was asked to describe a time when I led a project, and I talked about the school newspaper. Third, they enquired about my plans for July and wanted to know whether I could travel. Then they asked what I would do if the group did not agree, and I said that I would weigh up the options. Finally, I was asked to name one weakness, and I admitted that I sometimes stumble over my words when I am nervous. Overall, I felt confident and kept my composure. On reflection, my second answer was the strongest because it had a clear example. Next time I aim to improve my answer to the hypothetical question by adding a reason.
accepted: The panel asked me five questions. First, they wanted to know why I wanted the scholarship, and I explained my motivation. Then they asked what I would do if the group did not agree, and I said that I would weigh up the options. Finally, I was asked to name one weakness, and I admitted that I sometimes stumble over my words when I am nervous. Overall, I felt confident and kept my composure. On reflection, my second answer was the strongest because it had a clear example. Next time I aim to improve my answer to the hypothetical question by adding a reason.

I had an interview for the scholarship, and the panel asked me five questions. They wanted to know why I wanted the scholarship, and then I was asked to describe a time when I led a project. They also enquired about my plans for July and asked if I could travel. After that, they wanted to know what I would do if the group did not agree, and I was asked to name one weakness, which I found difficult to answer. Overall, I was not as nervous as I had feared. Looking back, my answer about the project was the strongest because it gave a concrete example. In future I aim to improve my answer to the hypothetical question by giving a clear reason, and I will practise keeping my composure when a question surprises me.

feedback.es: El relato recoge las cinco preguntas con estilo indirecto en pasado y cierra con una valoración de conjunto, lo mejor y un plan de mejora.

origin.text: Te hicieron cinco preguntas en una entrevista para una beca: 1) por qué quieres la beca; 2) cuéntame una vez en que lideraste un proyecto; 3) si podías viajar en julio; 4) qué harías si el grupo no estuviera de acuerdo; 5) nombra un punto débil. Cuenta qué te preguntaron (estilo indirecto, en pasado) y termina con una autoevaluación: cómo te sentiste en general, qué respondiste mejor y qué mejorarás la próxima vez.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender la hablante con su última frase.

choices.text: That her honesty turned an exam into a real conversation.
That the panel began to doubt whether she deserved the place.
That she felt the question had been unfair to her.

feedback.es: Al admitir un punto débil real, la conversación dejó de ser un examen y se volvió un diálogo: su sinceridad cambió el tono, no provocó dudas del comité ni lamento por su parte.

origin.audio: Honestly, I think the interview went better than I expected. They asked me to name a weakness, and instead of giving the usual answer about working too hard, I admitted that I tend to stumble over my words when I am nervous. The panel member smiled and asked how I was dealing with it. That is when I felt the conversation change: it stopped being an exam and started to feel like a real discussion.

prompt.es: ¿Qué informe es fiel a la pregunta original del comité?

choices.text: They demanded that I should start in September as soon as they offered me a place there.
They wanted to know whether I would be able to start in September if they offered me a place.
They asked why I would start in September if they offered me a place.

feedback.es: Es una pregunta de sí o no sobre una posibilidad: whether + would be able. Las otras la convierten en exigencia o en una pregunta con why.

origin.text: Original question from the panel: «Would you be able to start in September if we offered you a place?» Later, Sara's friend asks her what the panel wanted to know, and she answers in one sentence.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sara respiró hondo y mantuvo la compostura hasta el final de la respuesta.»

answer.text: composure

feedback.es: Keep your composure es la colocación para mantener la serenidad bajo presión; Sara respira y no pierde el control de su respuesta.

origin.text: When the panel asked an unexpected question, Sara felt her heart race, but she took a breath and kept her ___ until the end of her answer.

prompt.es: ¿Qué corrección se propone la hablante para la próxima entrevista?

choices.text: To speak for longer about what the whole team did.
To avoid questions about leading a team.
To focus on her own part and end with an outcome.

feedback.es: Su fallo fue hablar del equipo y no de ella; propone centrarse en su aportación y cerrar con un resultado, no hablar más del equipo ni evitar el tema.

origin.text: «On reflection, my weakest answer was the one about leading a team. I described what the team did rather than what I did, so the panel never saw my own part in it. Next time I aim to say what I did more clearly and to finish with a result.»

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué añade la hablante que ya había ahorrado dinero.

choices.text: To show that she was taking responsibility, not only asking for help.
To prove that the scholarship was no longer necessary for her.
To ask the panel to reduce the amount of money she needed.

feedback.es: Explica que ya ha ahorrado para no parecer indefensa: muestra responsabilidad propia. No dice que la beca sobre ni pide una cantidad menor.

origin.audio: The panel asked me why I wanted the scholarship. I said that I wanted to study music, and that my family could not pay for the course. I did not want to seem helpless, so I also explained that I had already saved some money myself and that the scholarship would simply make the rest possible.
